ihs_outlook.outlook_description: Corruption risks are likely to continue to fall as transitional authorities further investigate opaque spending under the long Bongo family rule.
Ongoing IMF funding and successful debt-for-nature swap efforts will support FX inflows and lower capital transfer risk.
Score affirmation: Likely continued control of government by the same Teke ethnic group will keep resentment lingering over their dominance of power.
The state oil company's heavy focus on former Assala Energy assets reduces the risk of other oil companies being pressured for a larger state share.
Score affirmation: The capacity of the judicial service and commercial courts is unlikely to change significantly while the transition plays out.
Likelihood of sustained high US interest rates and protectionism heightens the risk of depreciation, potentially leading to increased import costs.
Risks are likely to continue trending down given the end of the often volatile relationship between France and the Bongo dynasty.
The overwhelming vote in favour of a new constitution in November 2024 clears the way for the interim president to win election.
Inflation could be boosted by currency weakness due to the strength of the US Dollar.
The ongoing likely absence of civil unrest and strikes indicates that disruption to cargo and commercial activities will remain minimal.
Relations with Equatorial Guinea are likely to deteriorate prior to an expected court ruling in 2025 over ownership of disputed oil-rich islands.
The likely restoration of austerity measures in the bloated civil service increases the risk of widespread public sector strikes.
The interim government has given no sign of making changes affecting business operations and is likely to mark time in this respect until elections.
The 91.8% vote in favour of a new constitution in November 2024 underlines the lack of opposition to the interim president staying in power.
Higher domestic inflation and global outlook weakness impacts economic outlook.
The government is planning to overhaul the mining code in order to promote further investment in the rising sector.
Decrease in sovereign default risk amid easing external liquidity pressures and improved growth outlook.
Arrears owing to the World Bank and rising debt levels generally underline the risk of reduced funding for state institutions.
There is a rising risk of financial penalties being imposed on companies ahead of 2025 elections to help interim authorities meet spending promises.
Rising debt levels increase the probability of the government raising taxes, particularly with the transitional authorities promising high spending.
The continuing approval of a popular coup further reduces the already minimal risk of a politically motivated group emerging.
GDP per capita is forecast to increase by 7.2%.
